scope.title: From drone-to-satellite retrieval to reliable metric localization
scope.question: When does successful region retrieval fail to support a correct metric pose or pixel-to-map correspondence, and what evidence should trigger abstention?
scope.boundaries: 21 domain/adjacent papers, including 20 identifier-seeded papers and PAUL discovered through a new public search; five methodology foundations are separate. UAV imagery, orthophotos, off-nadir ambiguity, geometric refinement and selective prediction are included. Worldwide photo geolocation and terrestrial localization are adjacent evidence, not interchangeable UAV benchmarks.
scope.discovery: Local survey inventories supplied identifiers only. Titles, authors, dates and decisive claims were checked against freshly retrieved arXiv pages/full texts. Three independent arXiv terminology searches were screened; one was noisy. References in RIM, OrthoLoC and SkyReg informed the overlap analysis. This is a bounded, not systematic or exhaustive, search.
scope.date_policy: year/date denote first arXiv posting, not conference publication. Metadata and latest PDFs were fetched on the access date. SkyReg full text is explicitly v1 HTML. venue is null when no proceedings/publisher record was independently checked; author-reported venues are retained only in verification.
scope.evidence_policy: verified means the cited source supports the attributed claim, not that an experiment was independently reproduced. Full-paper evidence means selective examination of the cited full-text location, not cover-to-cover reading. Limitations include explicitly marked investigator inferences.
scope.blinding: Initial literature/tension/candidate generation inspected no pilot/benchmark* file, seeded novelty-overlap benchmark, or independent auditor output. After persistence, an independent auditor's correction message was received; listed corrections were checked directly in the already cached primary texts and are explicitly attributed in audit_updates. No audit artifact or benchmark file was opened. No agents were delegated.
scope.execution: Literature retrieval and CPU text extraction only. No models, training, GPU experiments, paid APIs or scientific benchmark runs.

papers.title: University-1652: A Multi-view Multi-source Benchmark for Drone-based Geo-localization
papers.task: Retrieve a target building across synthetic drone, satellite and ground views.
papers.relevance: Establishes an important drone retrieval benchmark but its target identity is not a camera pose or a building-corner correspondence.
papers.contribution: Multi-platform building dataset and CNN retrieval baseline.
papers.mechanism: View-invariant descriptor learning; building identity supplies the retrieval supervision.
limitations: Synthetic Google Earth drone views; real-flight transfer is a different evidence requirement.
Investigator inference: correct building retrieval alone does not establish metric pose or local feature accuracy.
papers.evaluation: Section 3.2 and Table 1: building-disjoint train/test identities; Recall@K and average precision, including drone-to-satellite and reverse retrieval.

evidence.claim: Drone views are generated using a synthetic camera rather than collected as an unrestricted real-flight pose benchmark.
Its evaluation unit is building identity, with retrieval metrics rather than 6-DoF pose accuracy.

papers.task: Estimate UAV location by retrieving geographically tagged satellite images.
papers.relevance: Directly relevant to the user's reduced DenseUAV motivation; that private preliminary result was not verified.
papers.contribution: Densely sampled low-altitude real UAV data, transformer/metric-learning baseline and distance-sensitive retrieval evaluation.

papers.title: Sample4Geo: Hard Negative Sampling For Cross-View Geo-Localisation
papers.task: Cross-view geographic image retrieval.
papers.relevance: Strong simple retrieval control; hard negatives address confusing regions but not metric geometric verification.
papers.contribution: Simplified shared-backbone contrastive training with geographic and dynamic visual hard negatives.
papers.mechanism: Symmetric InfoNCE, geographically nearby initial negatives, then embedding-neighbor dynamic similarity sampling.
limitations: Investigator inference: retrieval-discriminative training does not guarantee local feature equivariance.
Geographic positives/negatives must be redefined carefully when multiple tiles overlap one query.
papers.evaluation: Retrieval benchmarks and same-area/cross-area settings; full-paper methodology §§3.2-3.4 examined, no fresh reproduction.

evidence.claim: The method deliberately uses an off-the-shelf architecture rather than special view-specific adaptation.
Hard negatives use geographic proximity and subsequently dynamic embedding similarity.

verification.read: Abstract and methodology pp.3-4.

papers.title: InfoGeo: Information-Theoretic Object-Centric Learning for Cross-View Generalizable UAV Geo-Localization
papers.task: Generalizable UAV-to-satellite retrieval under region/weather changes.
papers.relevance: A strong semantic invariance mechanism that must not be mistaken for identifiable corner correspondences.
papers.contribution: Object-centric structural alignment expressed through an information-bottleneck formulation.
papers.mechanism: Latent slots, cross-view structural relations and suppression of view-specific signals.
limitations: Appendix reports degradation at higher altitude from concept scalability/noisy object signals.
Investigator inference: object slots and structural affinity do not establish dense metric correspondence.
papers.evaluation: Cross-view retrieval, ablations and transfer settings; only the inspected SUES-200/high-altitude and weather passages are claimed here.

evidence.claim: The mechanism uses sparse latent slots to represent underlying concepts.
Its own appendix identifies object-centric scalability as an altitude-dependent limitation.

verification.read: Abstract; method p.3; ablation p.8; appendix p.21.

papers.title: Pixel-wise Geo-registration of Drone and Satellite Images
papers.task: Assign per-pixel geodetic coordinates to drone imagery using a georeferenced satellite image.
papers.relevance: Direct prior art against a purportedly new dense UAV-to-satellite georegistration task.
papers.contribution: Pixel-level supervision/benchmark and 3D-reconstruction-based warping.
papers.mechanism: Lift image pixels into shared reconstructed 3D, compose query/reference mappings, then interpolate reference GPS. Section 3.4 also predicts per-pixel confidence and uses confidence-weighted pointmap regression.
limitations: Accessed abstract title and v1 HTML title differ; v1 says Pixel-wise Geo-registration of Drone Images. Do not silently treat this as a publication-title match.
Dense geodetic error is aggregated by a median within each image; this does not certify every building corner.
Source reports robustness to occlusions; this is not proof of correct invisible-surface identification.
No independent reproduction, dataset access check or uncertainty calibration was performed.
papers.evaluation: HTML §5.1 defines per-pixel Haversine error, per-image median geodetic error, median-GPS image localization and threshold recall. §5.2 compares retrieval, sparse/dense matching and geometry-aware approaches; §5.4 examines training subsets.

evidence.claim: Existing work already provides dense pixel-wise geodetic supervision and a geometry-aware cross-view method.
The dense metric summarizes each image using median per-pixel error.
evidence.quote: we assign the median error as the geodetic error

evidence.claim: The authors report planar-homography breakdown in urban scenes with tall structures and strong parallax.
evidence.quote: planar homography assumptions often break down

evidence.claim: SkyReg already predicts pixelwise confidence and trains with confidence-weighted regression; this is a required baseline for selective anchor quality.

papers.title: Fine-Grained Cross-View Geo-Localization Using a Correlation-Aware Homography Estimator
papers.task: Estimate fine geographic location/orientation from a ground image and satellite crop.
papers.relevance: Shows that robust learned homography refinement is already established adjacent prior art.

papers.title: OrthoLoC: UAV 6-DoF Localization and Calibration Using Orthographic Geodata
papers.task: UAV 6-DoF localization and camera calibration from orthographic geodata.

tensions.title: Retrieval success is not a metric-pose certificate
tensions.observation: Building/region recall, distance-sensitive retrieval and true geographic pose accuracy answer different questions. This is a metric-task mismatch, not a contradiction between leaderboard numbers.
evidence: university1652: PDF p.4 Recall@K/AP and building identity
denseuav: PDF p.2 SDM motivation
rim: PDF p.51 solver output versus pose correctness
explanations: Correct semantic identity may permit many camera locations or correspondences.
Gallery discretization and scene geometry introduce error not measured by identity recall.
tensions.unresolved: How often correct retrieval masks metric failure on the user's actual DenseUAV subset is unmeasured.

tensions.title: Positive overlap is not unique point correspondence
tensions.observation: VIGOR and Game4Loc explicitly allow multiple/partial positives, while dense registration requires a specific spatial mapping. Therefore binary same-region labels cannot resolve every local ambiguity.
evidence: vigor: PDF p.2 semi-positive samples and offsets
game4loc: PDF pp.2,4 intersection-ratio supervision
skyreg: HTML §5.1 per-pixel geodetic evaluation
explanations: Several tiles can be correct retrieval answers.
Only part of an oblique view may have a visible counterpart in the orthophoto.
tensions.unresolved: Whether explicitly preserving multiple geographic hypotheses improves accepted-pose risk beyond calibrated top-1 baselines.

tensions.title: Off-nadir identity can survive when metric observability fails
tensions.observation: OffNadirLoc addresses extreme-view retrieval, whereas OrthoLoC and SkyReg examine different geometric outputs. Strong off-nadir recall does not establish observable facade-to-map correspondences.
evidence: offnadirloc: PDF pp.3,6 rendering and retrieval protocol
ortholoc: PDF p.10 covisibility and corrupted-match limitations
skyreg: HTML §5.2 parallax discussion
explanations: A facade can identify a building while remaining absent from the overhead view.
Occlusion, relief and perspective produce geometric uncertainty even with correct semantic identity.
tensions.unresolved: No matched cross-paper experiment in this pilot separates semantic recognition from surface observability.

tensions.title: Invariance useful for retrieval can remove local precision
tensions.observation: InfoGeo compresses view-specific clutter into object-centric structure; RoMa explicitly adds fine features to robust coarse features and treats coarse ambiguity as multimodal.
evidence: infogeo: PDF p.3 slots and p.21 altitude limitation
roma: PDF p.2 Figure 2 coarse multimodality/fine refinement
mast3r: PDF p.2 repetitive-pattern motivation
explanations: View-invariant semantic similarity and spatial equivariance are not identical objectives.
Repeated structures can remain indistinguishable after strong semantic pooling.
tensions.unresolved: This is a mechanistic hypothesis, not proof that InfoGeo features are intrinsically unsuitable for matching.

tensions.title: Useful homographies still have scene-dependent validity
tensions.observation: Correlation-aware alignment and AdHoP support homographies, while SkyReg reports breakdown under tall-structure parallax. These settings are compatible, not mutually contradictory.
evidence: cahomo: PDF §3.1 spherical transform
ortholoc: PDF p.2 quasi-planar preconditioning; p.10 failure with corrupted matches
skyreg: HTML §5.2 urban parallax
explanations: Planar or locally quasi-planar surfaces can be well modeled; a single plane cannot represent every elevated/occluded surface.
Improved initialization and a correct scene model solve different failure modes.
tensions.unresolved: Whether a cheap geometry-sensitivity diagnostic detects model violation better than inlier residuals.

tensions.title: Predicted 3D structure still needs geographic anchoring
tensions.observation: VGGT/MASt3R supply geometry, but RIC-Loc uses known reference poses and OrthoLoC uses DSM-backed map coordinates to recover externally anchored pose.
evidence: vggt: abstract predicted geometry
ricloc: PDF p.4 posed-reference map assumptions
ortholoc: PDF pp.4,7 DSM lifting
explanations: Scene-relative coordinate predictions are not a geographic datum.
Scale, elevation and camera calibration can remain coupled.
tensions.unresolved: How datum/DSM errors interact with matching uncertainty on the intended real deployment.

tensions.title: Closed-gallery protocols omit the need to say no
tensions.observation: RIM explicitly excludes unmapped construction cases and lacks calibrated rejection; overlapping-reference retrieval benchmarks generally evaluate localization when map support exists.
evidence: rim: PDF p.27 temporal drift and no confidence estimator; p.28 proposed confidence fusion
game4loc: paired partial-overlap construction
ricloc: risk-coverage methodology
explanations: No valid reference is a different state from a difficult valid reference.
Solver-compatible correspondences may fit the wrong building or obsolete map.
tensions.unresolved: Empirical risk control under natural map absence/temporal change; removing true gallery entries is only a stress test, not realistic temporal-change validation.

tensions.title: Failure ranking is not calibrated risk under shift
tensions.observation: RIC-Loc is explicit that its covariance is a failure-ranking approximation; PAUL's uncertainty concerns training pairs; LightGlue's adaptivity concerns pairwise matching. None should be silently interpreted as a guaranteed UAV geographic error bound.
evidence: ricloc: PDF pp.15,20 approximate covariance and shared hypotheses
paul: PDF p.2 noisy-pair formulation
lightglue: abstract adaptivity and PDF p.5 training domain
explanations: Different uncertainty targets and calibration populations.
Geographic or acquisition shift invalidates naive exchangeability assumptions.
tensions.unresolved: Whether geographic grouping improves empirical transfer without collapsing coverage; no distribution-free claim under arbitrary shift is justified.

tensions.title: More candidates can repeat the same wrong evidence
tensions.observation: RIC-Loc admits shared-pass dependence; RoMa models multimodal correspondence; repeated structures motivate MASt3R. Thus candidate count alone need not represent independent pose evidence.
evidence: ricloc: PDF p.15 independence approximation and reference-selection future work
roma: PDF p.2 multimodal coarse matching
mast3r: PDF p.2 repetitive patterns
explanations: Nearby overlapping tiles may share the same wrong structure.
Reference descriptors and predicted geometry may inherit common backbone errors.
tensions.unresolved: A footprint-based dependence proxy may be too weak or redundant with existing dispersion/residual scores.

tensions.title: Coarse-to-fine integration is established; useful novelty must be narrower
tensions.observation: HF-Net, UnifyGeo and RIM already connect global retrieval with local/geometric localization, with progressively different assumptions and resource trade-offs.
evidence: hfnet: PDF pp.2-3 multitask distillation and PnP
unifygeo: PDF pp.2,6 shared objectives and reranking
rim: PDF p.6 shared-token distillation; p.28 future work
explanations: Engineering combinations can be useful without being a new scientific contribution.
Controlled failure analysis or evidence-selection behavior is narrower than merely adding a matcher to retrieval.
tensions.unresolved: Whether any remaining difference survives classical active localization and selective-prediction prior art searches.

opportunities.title: Geographic dependence-aware abstention for retrieved UAV pose hypotheses
opportunities.question: Does treating overlapping map candidates as correlated evidence reduce confidently wrong geographic poses at useful coverage, beyond existing confidence-fusion and pose-dispersion baselines?
opportunities.hypothesis: Candidate footprint concentration and leave-one-footprint-cluster-out pose instability identify wrong-building consensus that retrieval margins and within-fit residuals miss.
opportunities.contribution: Potentially a narrowly defined evidence-dependence diagnostic plus geographically held-out selective-risk evaluation, not the invention of confidence fusion, consensus or abstention.
opportunities.significance: A finite but incorrect pose is operationally different from retrieval failure; a cheap reject decision could prevent downstream map/trajectory corruption.

prior_art.overlap: Multiple hypotheses, robust consensus, covariance/dispersion scores, residual-consistency inflation, common-mode scale terms and full-set ineligible-query behavior already exist; dependence is explicitly acknowledged.
prior_art.difference: Only map-footprint-specific residual dependence of UAV satellite candidates remains a possible difference. All-query evaluation, generic covariance inflation and common-mode scale correction are not differences; novelty remains unresolved.

prior_art.overlap: Already proposes calibrated fusion of retrieval, correspondence, PnP and temporal signals.
prior_art.difference: Only a demonstrable gain from dependence-aware grouping beyond that full feature set could remain; generic confidence fusion is rejected.

prior_art.overlap: Uncertainty-aware handling of imperfect cross-view correspondences.
prior_art.difference: PAUL handles noisy training supervision; proposed target is test-time metric failure and abstention.
Geographic pose-risk assessment across retrieved references is distinct from pairwise coarse matching, but requires empirical verification.

experiment.hypothesis: At matched accepted-query coverage, dependence-aware scores reduce large geographic errors relative to a calibrated baseline using retrieval margin, inlier count, spatial support, residual and pose dispersion.
datasets: Primary: small geographically separated OrthoLoC subset with geodata and camera truth, after access/license/annotation preflight.
Transfer: UAV-VisLoc for horizontal location error only; do not pretend its metadata supplies full 6-DoF truth.
Use existing naturally unsupported cases if available; deliberate true-tile removal is a separately labeled stress test only.
baselines: Retrieval-margin ranking
Inlier count, spatial support and robust residual ranking
Pose-hypothesis dispersion
Logistic confidence fusion of all above
RIC-Loc dispersion/covariance including common-mode scale and residual-consistency inflation, with its full-set handling, on compatible posed-reference data; otherwise explicitly not comparable
Random/oracle ranking diagnostic bounds
metrics: Coverage at predeclared empirical 10% failure target
Accepted-query median and p95 horizontal error

config.geographic_split: Group by non-overlapping map regions/flight sequences; no neighboring frame may cross calibration/test. Fit score parameters on one subset, choose threshold on a second, freeze before held-out geography.
config.dependence_proxy: Group overlapping candidate footprints; compare distinct-support count and leave-one-cluster-out pose displacement. Ablate each proxy separately.
config.fallback: Use cached approved matcher outputs if present. Otherwise CPU ORB+RANSAC/PnP provides only a mechanism-screening baseline, not a RoMa/RIM replication. If sufficient independent regions or truth are unavailable, record blocked rather than inventing examples.

experiment.compute: 1-2 researcher days; CPU postprocessing of cached outputs or bounded classical matches, <=8 CPU-hours, <=16 GB RAM. No GPU execution authorized. Any learned-feature extraction requires a separately approved budget.
experiment.success: Predeclared screening rule: >=10% relative AURC reduction versus full confidence fusion and a nonnegative clustered-bootstrap improvement interval on held-out geography, while retaining >=50% supported-query coverage. These are proposed decision thresholds, not results.
experiment.falsification: Stop if the proxy adds no held-out ranking value, improvement vanishes at matched coverage, only impossible-map removal drives the effect, or coverage is below 50%. Calibration under arbitrary distribution shift is not claimed.

gaps: Need broader classical correlated-estimator, selective-localization and group-calibration prior-art audit.
Footprint overlap is only a proxy for error dependence.
Natural map-change cases and all-query failures may be unavailable.
No implementation or data-license preflight has been performed.

priority.decision: Best first diagnostic to audit, not a validated new method.
priority.basis: Directly evidenced reliability gap; cheapest computation; high novelty risk from RIC-Loc and RIM.

venue.candidate: CVPR/ECCV or robotics-localization venue only after a real technical distinction and multi-geography evidence
venue.minimum_evidence: Actual correlated-evidence failure mechanism, fair strong confidence baselines, all-query coverage, two independent real geographic transfers and reproducible failure cases.

opportunities.title: Geometry-sensitivity gating for off-nadir pixel-to-map anchors
opportunities.question: Can sensitivity to plausible elevation and camera perturbations identify locally untrustworthy map anchors that have small image reprojection residuals?
opportunities.hypothesis: At large off-nadir angles, DSM/height sensitivity and homography-versus-3D disagreement predict tail geodetic error better than residual/inlier confidence alone.
opportunities.contribution: Potentially an observability-oriented diagnostic for which anchors should be withheld, evaluated on existing georegistration data. Not a new dense-registration task, generic 3D matcher or new benchmark.
opportunities.significance: A correct image median can hide wrong individual structure anchors; downstream metric use needs localized evidence quality.

prior_art.overlap: Already supplies dense georegistration, nonplanar reconstruction, pixelwise evaluation and predicted per-pixel confidence trained by confidence-weighted regression.
prior_art.difference: Only additional predictive value of map/height sensitivity beyond existing point-confidence and analytic uncertainty propagation could remain; dense GPS or pixel-confidence prediction are not differences.

prior_art.overlap: DSM-backed pose, covisibility analysis and AdHoP directly address perspective/orthographic geometry.
prior_art.difference: Would need to show sensitivity predicts unreliability beyond AdHoP, residuals and known covisibility, rather than repackage its robustness analyses.

prior_art.overlap: Geometry-aware image alignment with a learned homography estimator.
prior_art.difference: Targets the validity of anchors under nonplanar scene/model uncertainty rather than improved homography estimation.
Requires geographic anchoring and a selective geodetic-error question, not simply attaching a 3D matcher.

experiment.hypothesis: A perturbation-derived map sensitivity score reduces accepted-anchor p95 geodetic error beyond reprojection residual and match confidence at the same anchor coverage.
datasets: OrthoLoC DSM/DOP, pointmap/mesh and camera-truth subset; distinguish reconstruction-derived same-domain references from external cross-domain DOP+DSM.
SkyReg-Bench public subset only if depth/camera/geodetic annotations and access terms are actually available; otherwise mark pixelwise transfer blocked.
baselines: Homography with RANSAC
DSM-lifted PnP
AdHoP if public implementation is usable
Match confidence plus reprojection residual
Analytic ray-surface height sensitivity and first-order covariance propagation
SkyReg and MASt3R existing predicted point-confidence maps
Cached RoMa/MASt3R/SkyReg predictions if approved and available; do not call classical matches these methods
metrics: Per-anchor local metric median/p95 and threshold recall; geodetic error only when a verified global transform is available
Image-level median-GPS error only for globally georeferenced data, kept separate
Risk-coverage by off-nadir, terrain relief and covisibility

config.method: Keep observed matches fixed. Re-estimate or propagate map coordinates under symmetric DSM-height perturbations; rank by geodetic displacement and H/PnP disagreement. Use ground-truth pose/depth only for scoring and stratification, never for the prediction score.
config.ablation: Residual alone; sensitivity alone; combined; low-relief versus high-relief; matched anchor count. Use actual surface/visibility labels only where supplied, never infer them as truth from a model.
config.split: Tune thresholds on separate geographic sites; bootstrap at site/query level, not independent pixels.
config.stop_condition: If DSM and pixelwise truth cannot be obtained in half a day, stop as data-blocked; no synthetic truth substitution.

experiment.compute: 2-3 researcher days, <=12 CPU-hours and <=16 GB RAM for bounded geometry perturbations using cached/classical matches. No GPU run; learned outputs require separate permission if unavailable.
experiment.success: Screening criterion: >=20% relative reduction in p95 anchor error at >=50% coverage versus the strongest residual, existing point-confidence and analytic ray/covariance baselines on held-out sites; consistent direction on relief strata and separately reported external-DSM transfer. Threshold is prospective, not observed.
experiment.falsification: Reject if simple off-nadir/relief covariates, analytic propagation or existing point confidence explain the gain; if inaccessible ground-truth geometry is required; if no pixelwise truth exists; if gains disappear at matched coverage or on external DSM; or if the claim depends on calling local coordinates global GPS.

gaps: Classical photogrammetric error propagation, observability and terrain-intersection uncertainty may already establish the mechanism.
Pixelwise registration is not equivalent to visible shared-surface correspondence.
DSM accuracy and ground-truth geodetic noise must bound any precision claim.
SkyReg v1/latest-title discrepancy and data-release status require follow-up.

priority.decision: Conditional diagnostic; likely useful for understanding failures, high risk of classical prior art.
priority.basis: Clear geometry-task mismatch but expensive annotation/access uncertainty.

venue.candidate: CVPR/ICCV only with a distinct mechanism beyond standard uncertainty propagation
venue.minimum_evidence: Real dense geodetic truth, explicit visibility/map-error analysis, strong geometry baselines and transfer beyond a single rendered dataset.

opportunities.title: Fixed-budget candidate selection by independent geometric support
opportunities.question: At the same number of expensive pair matches, does selecting geographically diverse, geometrically supported references outperform retrieval-score top-K and learned reranking?
opportunities.hypothesis: Some top-ranked candidates redundantly cover the same ambiguous structure; cheap support/conditioning proxies can allocate a fixed matching budget more effectively.
opportunities.contribution: At most a resource-controlled marginal-utility analysis and narrowly specified selector; generic retrieval-plus-matching, diversity selection and geometry-aware reranking are rejected as novelty claims.
opportunities.significance: Useful if edge localization needs a small fixed matching budget and additional similar candidates do not improve metric success.

prior_art.overlap: Geometry-aware reference selection using viewpoint diversity, track support and conditioning is explicitly future work.
prior_art.difference: No clear novelty established. Only a distinct fixed-budget satellite-footprint selection result might remain after a full audit.

prior_art.overlap: Top-K matching, geometric reranking, efficient shared features and speed comparisons already exist.
prior_art.difference: Select candidates before expensive dense matching under a strictly equal budget; not rerank using already-paid full geometry.

prior_art.overlap: Joint learning and dedicated reranking improve candidate references for metric localization.
prior_art.difference: Frozen training-free selection emphasizing independent geometric support rather than a new shared model.

prior_art.overlap: Retrieval is followed by explicit clustering of candidate frames according to shared 3D covisibility before geometric pose checking.
prior_art.difference: Footprint-based grouping may merely approximate established covisibility grouping; a specifically distinct fixed-budget marginal-utility result is needed, not generic hierarchy or candidate clustering.

experiment.hypothesis: At exactly two or five costly pair matches per query, a selector improves end-to-end metric success over top-K and simple geographic nonmaximum suppression without an oracle.
datasets: UAV-VisLoc for non-oracle map retrieval and horizontal position.
OrthoLoC only if a real candidate gallery can be formed without using paired ground truth to select references; otherwise paired data cannot test this hypothesis.
baselines: Top-K descriptor score
Random selection within top-20
Geographic footprint nonmaximum suppression
HF-Net-style covisibility grouping where the map supports it
Cheap inlier-count ranking
RIM/UnifyGeo style geometry reranking with every match counted in the budget
Oracle candidate selection labeled as an unattainable bound
metrics: Matched-pair count and measured CPU/GPU latency separately

config.selector: Use only retrieval score, map footprints and capped low-resolution classical support probes before allocating full matches. Charge every probe to the timing/budget ledger. Greedily add candidates with new spatial support; compare directly with simple geographic NMS.
config.split: Geographic calibration/test split; fixed hyperparameters before held-out evaluation.
config.ablation: Score only, diversity only, support only, combined. Report both correct-candidate-available conditional diagnostic and non-oracle end-to-end results.
config.fallback: If public retrieval/matching caches are absent, bounded CPU ORB descriptors/matches can only falsify the redundancy mechanism; no learned-system superiority claim.

experiment.compute: 1-2 researcher days; <=8 CPU-hours for bounded cached-output/classical-match analysis; no training and no GPU execution. Full learned model comparison needs later approval.
experiment.success: Screening criterion: >=5 percentage-point absolute metric-success gain versus top-K at matched budget, plus positive gain over geographic NMS on held-out geography; count all selection overhead.
experiment.falsification: Reject if geographic NMS matches performance, additional probes erase the budget benefit, oracle gallery information is needed, or gains occur only in paired-reference evaluation.

gaps: Strong likely overlap with active localization, viewpoint selection and optimal experimental design not exhaustively searched.
RIC-Loc already articulates the high-level idea.
Dataset gallery construction and map footprint availability need verification.
This is the weakest novelty candidate and should be dropped rather than inflated if a simple selector suffices.

priority.decision: Hold: likely engineering baseline, not currently a defensible research contribution.
priority.basis: Cheap falsification but very high known conceptual overlap.

venue.minimum_evidence: A non-obvious selection principle with end-to-end real-data gains beyond classical diversity/conditioning baselines under a complete compute ledger.
